title: NAC Authentication Trending
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'NAC Authentication Trending' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_nac_authentication_trending` (UC-17.1.1), SOC dashboard panel "Network — NAC Authentication Trending", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:auth' where `status` satisfies detection threshold for UC-17.1.1 ('NAC Authentication Trending'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:auth` events where `status` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.1.

dataSources: RADIUS/ISE authentication logs Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk_TA_cisco-ise`, HPE Aruba ClearPass syslog, Forescout CounterACT syslog — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:auth"
| eval status=if(match(message,"PASS"),"success","failure")
| timechart span=1h count by status
description: Authentication success/failure trends reveal infrastructure issues (certificate problems, RADIUS outages) and security events.
value: Authentication success/failure trends reveal infrastructure issues (certificate problems, RADIUS outages) a.... Timely UC-17.1.1 alerting on 'NAC Authentication Trending' reduces unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Forward ISE PSN syslog (TCP/UDP 514) to a Heavy Forwarder. Configure `props.conf`/`transforms.conf` for field extraction of `AuthenticationPolicy`, `Passed/Failed`, `Calling-Station-ID`, and `NAS-IP-Address`. Alert on failure-rate spikes vs the 7-day same-hour baseline, segmented by `nas_ip` or `location`, to distinguish localized AP/switch issues from systemic RADIUS problems.
visualization: Line chart (auth success/failure rates), Bar chart (failures by location), Pie chart (auth method distribution).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  by Authentication.user, Authentication.action, Authentication.src span=1h
| sort - count
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'NAC Authentication Trending'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:auth` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco ISE: Splunk Add-on for Cisco ISE (Splunkbase) with `sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog`. Aruba ClearPass: Splunk Add-on for Aruba ClearPass with `sourcetype=aruba:clearpass`. Forescout: syslog integration with `sourcetype=forescout:syslog`.
• Data in `index=nac`. Key ISE fields: `UserName`, `IdentityGroup`, `EndPointPolicy`, `AuthenticationStatus` (Passed/Failed), `NetworkDeviceName` (switch/WLC), `NAS-Port-Type` (Ethernet/Wireless), `CallingStationID` (MAC), `FailureReason`, `AuthorizationPolicyMatchedRule`.
• RADIUS authentication logs from the NAC server. ISE sends syslog messages with IDs 5200 (auth passed), 5400 (auth failed), 5405 (RADIUS request dropped).
• Create a `nac_network_devices.csv` lookup: `nas_ip,device_name,location,building,floor` for mapping Network Access Servers to physical locations.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
For Cisco ISE: Administration > System > Logging > Remote Logging Targets > add the HF IP, TCP 514, syslog format. Enable PASSED_AUTHENTICATIONS and FAILED_ATTEMPTS log categories.

Verify:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" earliest=-1h
| stats count by AuthenticationStatus
```
You should see both Passed and Failed. If only Passed: failed authentication logging may be disabled. If nothing: check syslog connectivity and the ISE logging configuration.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Authentication trending:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" earliest=-7d
| eval status=case(match(AuthenticationStatus, "(?i)pass"), "Passed", match(AuthenticationStatus, "(?i)fail"), "Failed", 1==1, "Other")
| timechart span=1h count by status
| eval success_rate=round(Passed/(Passed+Failed)*100, 1)
```

Understanding this SPL: Tracks hourly authentication volume and success rate. The success rate is the primary health indicator. A drop below 95% warrants investigation — it could mean a misconfigured policy affecting a group of users, a certificate issue, or an infrastructure problem (RADIUS server degraded). Daily patterns are normal (low at night, high at business start). Anomalies against this pattern are significant.

Failure analysis:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" earliest=-24h
| where match(AuthenticationStatus, "(?i)fail")
| stats count as failures dc(CallingStationID) as devices dc(UserName) as users by FailureReason
| sort - failures
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) In ISE: Operations > RADIUS > Live Logs. Compare the pass/fail ratio with Splunk for the last hour.
(b) In ClearPass: Monitoring > Live Monitoring > Access Tracker.
(c) Intentionally fail an authentication (wrong password) and verify it appears in Splunk.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard ("NAC — Authentication Health"):
• Row 1 — Single-value: "Auth success rate (%)", "Failures (24h)", "Unique devices".
• Row 2 — Timechart: pass/fail over 7 days.
• Row 3 — Table: failure reasons with count, affected devices, affected users.

Alert: Trigger when auth success rate drops below 90% in any 1h window. This is a broad indicator of NAC infrastructure or policy issues.

Runbook:
1. **Success rate drop + single failure reason** — A specific policy or certificate issue. Check the FailureReason for the root cause.
2. **Success rate drop + many failure reasons** — RADIUS server overload or infrastructure issue. Check ISE node health.
3. **Gradual failure increase** — Certificate approaching expiry (clients failing EAP-TLS). Check the RADIUS server certificate.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No auth events** — ISE logging categories may be disabled. Check Administration > Logging > Logging Categories > ensure PASSED_AUTHENTICATIONS and FAILED_ATTEMPTS are enabled.
• **`FailureReason` empty** — The syslog format may not include failure details. Switch to 'detailed' syslog format in ISE.
• **Events delayed** — ISE batches syslog messages. Increase the ISE syslog buffer flush interval or switch to pxGrid for real-time data.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the success rate of devices trying to get on our network, and when more start failing than usual, we investigate whether there is a problem with our access rules or security system.
hardware: Cisco ISE 3515/3595/3615/3655/3695, ISE Virtual Appliance; HPE Aruba ClearPass C1000/C2000/C3000, ClearPass Virtual Appliance; Forescout CounterACT CT-xxxx, eyeExtend
